title: The Cipher of Windrow House
premise: Ada Montrose, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has a private habit of solving the deaths the police file away as accidents. When a stranger is found dead in Windrow House wearing clothes stolen from Ada's own closet, she realizes someone knows her secret methods — and is using them to frame her. Following a cipher hidden in the cathedral's centuries-old burial ledger, she uncovers a conspiracy reaching back to her predecessor's disappearance, and to the locked crypt itself. In the end, Ada must choose between protecting the one person who showed her loyalty and exposing a truth that will destroy the institution that gave her a home.
about_author: E. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing English cathedral archives before turning to fiction. Known for quiet, meticulous mysteries, Iversen writes about people who find belonging in old buildings and dangerous truths in old paper.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She introduces her nightly routine in the cathedral archive, the crypt sealed since 1911, and her private notebook of 'accidents' she has quietly solved. Emotional beat: the comfort of order, shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Police summon her to Windrow House, where a dead man wears her own missing cardigan and scarf. Detective Inspector Quill, half-suspicious, notes the coincidence aloud. Beat: fear arrives dressed as familiarity.

chapters.title: What the Closet Gave Up
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She searches her flat and finds the theft was precise — only items with sentimental value taken. A neighbor saw nothing, but a ledger page from the archive is missing. Beat: violation; the killer knows her intimately.

chapters.title: Quill's Patience
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: DI Quill reviews Ada's history near three past deaths. He doesn't accuse; he watches. Beat: the hunter's calm dread — Ada realizes her record makes her either witness or suspect.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Lies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Comparing the burial ledger against gravestones, she finds entries that don't match any interment — dates forming a pattern. Beat: the thrill of the hunt rekindled through fear.

chapters.title: Windrow House Opens
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She visits the victim's home and meets his sister, Ruth, who reveals he'd been researching the cathedral's 1911 closure of the crypt. Beat: grief shared becomes alliance formed.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, Revisited
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with flashback texture. She lays out her three solved cases and sees they all connect to families named in the false ledger entries. Beat: cold recognition — the pattern was always there.

chapters.title: The Predecessor's Box
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hidden behind the archive shelving, she finds her vanished predecessor's box: photographs, a partial key, and a note reading 'count the Sundays.' Beat: inheritance of danger.

chapters.title: Counting Sundays
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The false dates align with Sundays when a particular verger logged the crypt as inspected — inspections that never happened. Someone has used the crypt for decades. Beat: vertigo beneath familiar stone.

chapters.title: Ruth's Warning
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth receives an anonymous note telling her to stop her brother's work, and hides it from Ada. Beat: loyalty tested by fear; the reader learns something Ada doesn't.

chapters.title: The Verger's Grandson
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She traces the verger's line to Mr. Ellery, the cathedral's beloved head verger, who deflects her questions with warmth. Beat: charm as camouflage; doubt takes root in a trusted face.

chapters.title: Second Body
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The neighbor who 'saw nothing' is found drowned, and this time the staged scene points clumsily at Ada. Quill can no longer protect her from suspicion. Beat: the net tightens.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Quill interviews Ada for hours; she finally shows him her private notebook. He believes her — mostly. Beat: reluctant trust forged between two careful people.

chapters.title: The Cipher in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The ledger's illuminated capitals, read by the Sunday-count, spell out names and amounts — payments for silence about what lies in the crypt. Beat: revelation as betrayal; the church itself took money.

chapters.title: What Was Buried Twice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Records suggest the crypt holds not remains but documents: proof of a 1911 cover-up that enriched founding families, including the Windrows. Beat: history's weight becomes present danger.

chapters.title: Ellery's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ellery's POV. He reflects on his grandfather's oath and his own long guardianship, convincing himself every death served the cathedral. Beat: chilling tenderness; the antagonist fully humanized.

chapters.title: Ruth Disappears
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ruth vanishes after finding the final cipher page; a note in Ada's handwriting (forged) lures searchers elsewhere. Beat: desperation — the killer now writes in Ada's voice.

chapters.title: Into the Crypt
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Using the predecessor's key and the Sunday count, Ada opens the sealed crypt ahead of Quill, finding Ruth alive and the document cache — and Ellery waiting. Beat: terror and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: The Choice of Loyalties
chapters.summary: Climax, Ada's POV. Ellery offers Ada a place in the guardianship — belonging, purpose, protection — if the papers burn. Ruth begs her to choose truth. Beat: the book's thematic crux made literal.

chapters.title: Ashes and Arrests
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada pretends to agree, then triggers Quill's arrival; Ellery, rather than be taken, seals himself in the crypt with the burning papers. Beat: catharsis shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath at Windrow House
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Cases reopened, names cleared, Ada formally thanked and quietly warned. Quill admits he'd have believed her sooner if he'd been braver. Beat: earned respect, gently offered.

chapters.title: A New Page in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She catalogs the recovered documents honestly, enters the true names into the ledger, and accepts Ruth's friendship. The crypt stays open now. Beat: belonging found not in secrets kept, but in truth shared.
